section_1.title: Prerequisites: Visualizing Complex Roots
section_1.content: Briefly review the n-th roots of unity. Represent ω = e^(i*2π/n) as vectors pointing to the vertices of a regular n-gon on the complex unit circle. Emphasize the 'Filter Property': Σ ω^(jk) = n if n|k, and 0 otherwise.
section_1.example: Visual animation: A unit circle showing 4th roots of unity (1, i, -1, -i) spinning and canceling each other out when raised to a power not divisible by 4.

section_2.title: From Combinatorics to Polynomials
section_2.content: Introduce generating functions as a way to encode sequences. Connect the 'selection' of items to polynomial coefficients. Introduce the persona: 'The Inventory Robot' deciding how many apples and oranges to pack into a crate.
section_2.example: Robot packs x types of fruits: (1+x+x^2+...)^k represents choosing any number of fruits for k slots, encoded as the coefficients of P(x).

section_3.title: The Roots of Unity Filter (The Core Technique)
section_3.content: Explain how to extract the sum of coefficients a_k where k ≡ r (mod n). Show the formula: 1/n * Σ ω^(-rk) * P(ω^k). Use a visual sliding window overlaying the roots of unity onto the polynomial graph.
section_3.example: A squirrel collecting acorns: Finding the number of ways to pick a total count of acorns such that the count is a multiple of 3 (n=3) using P(x) = (1+x+x^2+x^3)^N.

section_4.title: Synthesis and Application
section_4.content: Walk through a step-by-step calculation: defining the polynomial, applying the roots of unity, simplifying the complex powers, and arriving at the final combinatorial result.
section_4.example: Final calculation for the squirrel: Using the sum of cubes of binomial coefficients filtered by mod 3 to count configurations where the total is 'balanced' (divisible by 3).
